scope: The structure of a cookbook principle artifact, a short, always-loaded statement of an engineering principle: its meta (frontmatter), its title heading, its one-paragraph statement, its actionable guidance, its change history, its length, and the parts of guide/introduction/conventions.md (The Standard, Roles) that govern a principle. Out of scope: RFC 2119 keyword case and the lint severity a keyword gives a finding (both owned by the sibling topic requirement-keywords).
research_type: How-to / troubleshooting (intent Do; domain technical writing and agent context; Product / how-to LOW-MEDIUM bar, Technical MEDIUM bar for agent-host documentation)

questions.text: Best practices: what is current best practice for this topic?
Known solutions: what solutions, patterns, libraries and tools already exist, and how do they compare?
Platform guidelines: what do the platform owners' own guidelines say, for each platform the topic touches (Apple, Android, Windows, web, the databases and runtimes concerned)?
The expert's view: if we hired an expert consultant in this topic, what would they tell us: what to do, what to avoid, and what people usually get wrong?

methodology.method: guidelines/researching/process/research-methodology-and-sources: orient and classify (technical writing; agent context), go to the authoritative sources for that domain (style-guide owners, documentation-framework authors, lint and schema tool documentation, agent-host vendor documentation, peer-reviewed or preprint studies of long-context instruction following), corroborate across independent sources, record provenance at generation time.
methodology.search_strategy: Targeted searches and direct fetches of each owner's documentation: Anthropic (Claude Code memory and best-practices pages, Agent Skills authoring best practices, prompting best practices, two engineering posts), the Agent Skills specification, OpenAI Codex AGENTS.md guide, GitHub Copilot repository instructions, Cursor rules, agents.md; Diataxis explanation page; Google developer documentation style guide (headings) and Google technical-writing course (paragraphs); Microsoft Writing Style Guide (top 10 tips, scannable content, lists); markdownlint rule docs (MD013, MD025, MD041, MD043, custom rules) raw from the project repository; Vale check docs (metric, occurrence, script); JSON Schema reference (required, const); Astro content collections; Keep a Changelog 1.1.0; PEP 1; Nygard's ADR post; NN/g inverted pyramid; Write the Docs docs-as-code; arXiv abstracts of Lost in the Middle and IFScale; Chroma's Context Rot report. Every page was fetched with curl and converted to text; every quote was copied from the fetched text.
methodology.inclusion: Primary: style-guide and framework owners' own pages, tool documentation for what the tool does, agent-host vendors' documentation for their own hosts, the research papers' own abstracts. Secondary only where no primary covers the point (NN/g, Write the Docs, Nygard's ADR post, Keep a Changelog, Chroma's vendor report), flagged in each trust basis.
methodology.exclusion: Search-result snippets; pages not fetched; blogs, SEO articles and forum posts; any claim without a fetched verbatim quote. Each claim cites only the page that holds its quote, so corroboration is recorded across claims (named in each trust basis and in the verdicts), not by stacking citations on one quote.
methodology.scoring: guidelines/researching/evidence/verification-and-trust-scoring: Authority 30 + Independent corroboration 25 + Accuracy/verifiability 20 + Currency 10 + Transparency 15, capped by the domain bar (Product / how-to LOW-MEDIUM; Technical MEDIUM for agent-host documentation); secondary sources scored at most 72; preprints and vendor reports at most 78; prior cookbook text 0.

summary: Outside practice supports the shape of a principle: required metadata checked by a schema (PEP 1's required preamble, JSON Schema required/const, Astro collection schemas, Agent Skills' required name and description), one title per document (Google; markdownlint MD025/MD041), the main point first (NN/g, Microsoft, Google), specific actionable guidance in bullets (Anthropic's context-engineering post and CLAUDE.md guidance, Cursor), and a dated, newest-first entry per version (Keep a Changelog). Four draft rules are not supported at the strength they state: no source requires the H1 to equal the frontmatter title (pf-title-heading), the statement-first and change-history practices are recommendations, not requirements (pf-statement and pf-change-history hold at SHOULD), and no source supports a ~50-line cap (pf-brevity). The evidence on length is real but sets budgets, not a per-principle number: agent hosts bound the always-loaded total (Claude Code: under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md truncated at 200 lines or 25KB; Codex: 32 KiB combined; Copilot's sample: two pages), bound on-demand skill bodies (SKILL.md under 500 lines, under 5000 tokens; Cursor rules under 500 lines), and studies show adherence and recall fall as context and instruction density grow (IFScale, Lost in the Middle, Chroma's Context Rot), with a bias toward earlier content. The Standard's role-separated content is consistent with Anthropic's progressive disclosure and evaluator-optimizer pattern, one source per topic with host warnings about contradictory instructions, and keeping the change history out of the compiled skills with Keep a Changelog's 'for humans, not machines'. Internal mechanics (the role vocabulary, every-part-roled, skill names, routing) cannot be confirmed by an outside source. New practice no rule covers: one title per document, state why, write only what the agent lacks, a summary that says what and when, newest-first history, tool-enforced format checks, a budget for the whole always-loaded set, and the most important guidance first.
open_questions: Which length figure the principle rule should name: the research supports no ~50-line per-principle cap; it supports a budget for everything always loaded (Claude Code's under-200-lines-per-file target) and an on-demand body bound (SKILL.md under 500 lines / under 5000 tokens). Whether principles are always loaded together (then the cap is the shared budget divided across the cookbook's principles, about 45 today) or load on demand as compiled skills (then the skill bound applies) is the owner's to decide.

Whether pf-frontmatter-complete's field list should match conventions.md's Field Definitions table, which marks approved-by and approved-date as required (written by /approve-artifact, not linted) while the draft list omits them.

Whether pf-title-heading keeps its exact-match MUST as an internal consistency check (tool-decidable) although no outside source requires it, or is restated as the single-title practice the sources support.
Whether pf-statement and pf-change-history stay MUST as definitions of the artifact type (internal design) or drop to the SHOULD their outside sources support.

How a principle's actionable bullets relate to Diataxis, which keeps instruction out of explanation: whether a principle is an explanation page with a short action list, or a separate artifact kind for which Diataxis is not the model.
limitations: No study found measures instruction following for a single document of a given line count; the length evidence is host guidance (file-level budgets) and studies of total context length or instruction density, none of which yields a per-principle line number.
Lost in the Middle and IFScale were read from their arXiv abstract pages, not their full PDFs; the findings cited are those the abstracts state.

No Apple, Android or Windows platform guidance bears on the structure of a Markdown principle file; the platform question was answered from the agent hosts' and style-guide owners' documentation the topic touches.

Absence claims (for example that markdownlint has no built-in document-length or title-equals-frontmatter rule) were not established; the research records only what the rule docs fetched say each rule does.
GitHub Copilot's 'no longer than 2 pages' appears inside a sample prompt GitHub publishes for generating instructions, not as a stated product limit.

Corroboration is recorded across separate claims (each quote is held by its one cited page), so most claims are marked single even where several independent publishers agree; the verdicts name the agreeing claims together.
license: MIT (this research record); quoted material remains under its sources' terms and is quoted for verification.
